title: Insulation options for leaseholders in a block of flats
subtitle: What a leaseholder can do individually and what requires building-wide consent
excerpt: Insulating a flat in a block is more constrained than insulating a house. External wall work requires the freeholder and usually all leaseholders. Internal wall insulation in your own flat is within your control but loses floor area. Loft insulation above the top flat and floor insulation below the ground flat are managed differently. Understanding the rules saves effort.
sourceNotes: Leasehold Advisory Service guidance on leaseholder alterations; Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Act 2002; PAS 2035 on whole-house retrofit and common parts; Energy Saving Trust advice for flats.

glossaryTerms.definition: Insulation applied to a solid masonry wall (no cavity), either on the internal face (IWI) or the external face (EWI).
Energy Company Obligation, a UK government scheme requiring larger energy suppliers to fund energy efficiency improvements in homes with low income or vulnerability qualifications.

content.text: A leaseholder in a block of flats does not own the external fabric of the building. The roof, external walls, and common areas are typically owned by the freeholder (or a management company). This shapes what an individual flat owner can insulate unilaterally and what requires building-wide agreement.
What you can do within your own flat
Internal wall insulation on the external walls inside your flat. A 50 to 75 mm

lining loses some floor area but needs no consent from other leaseholders. Check your lease for specific alteration clauses, some require written freeholder consent for internal works affecting structural elements.

Double or secondary glazing of your existing windows if the windows are within your demise (your lease boundary). Check the lease plan; many blocks include the windows in the common parts even where they are on your flat's facade.
Draught-proofing your flat's front door and window frames. This is maintenance, not alteration, and is within normal leaseholder rights.
Insulating the floor void inside your flat if there is a suspended timber floor over an unheated crawl space. This typically requires no external consent.

External wall insulation. Any work to the external fabric of the building requires freeholder consent. Most leases also require the agreement of all leaseholders if the work affects common parts. A whole-block EWI scheme is more viable than a single-flat scheme and typically achieves better grant funding.
Roof insulation. The loft above the top flat is typically common property. The top-flat leaseholder usually cannot insulate the roof without freeholder approval.
Ground-floor underfloor insulation where the void under the building is a common service area.

A whole-block retrofit is more cost-effective per flat than individual work. The freeholder can pass the cost of improvements through a Section 20 consultation (Landlord and Tenant Act). Grants through

and the Great British Insulation Scheme are available for whole-block solid-wall and loft insulation if the block qualifies on EPC and income criteria. A Retrofit Coordinator (required under PAS 2035 for publicly funded work) can assess and manage the scheme.

Commonhold blocks are much rarer in the UK. In a commonhold, the owners together control the common parts and can vote through improvements. There is no freeholder to block the decision. Retrofit decisions follow the commonhold community statement voting rules, not lease consent.

rows.symptom: Freeholder refuses consent for internal wall insulation citing lease terms
rows.cause: Some leases prohibit any alteration without consent; others specify that consent cannot be unreasonably withheld
rows.fix: Obtain the lease wording and seek advice from the Leasehold Advisory Service (free). If the alteration is reasonable and non-structural, refusal may be challengeable.

rows.symptom: Other leaseholders are not interested in a building-wide EWI scheme
rows.cause: Upfront cost and disruption concerns; lack of trust in the freeholder managing the process
rows.fix: Commission a whole-block energy survey and circulate the projected savings per flat. Grant funding that makes the scheme near-zero cost often unlocks agreement.
